findings.description: F001 requires a total SurfaceFamily mapping, but the proposed plan does not pin the exact family for every closed surface_class member. Ambiguous cells like external_integration, service_batch, and backend-derived surfaces can change consumer x surface validation outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit table assigning each closed surface_class to exactly one family before implementation locks.

findings.description: The journey.surfaces token mapping named in F001 lists web, backend, mcp_tool, cli_agent, and cli_human, but does not pin tokens for mobile_app or external_integration even though those are closed surface_class values and mobile human capture already exists.
findings.recommendation: Enumerate every accepted journey.surfaces token, including existing mobile and external-integration tokens, and map each to a closed surface_class.

findings.description: F002 states that agent_mcp_tool read_only success is satisfied by tool_call_transcript or contract_check, but the listed tests do not include the required unit-test-only mismatch and transcript-satisfied agent API/MCP cases from the journey contract.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit typing-rule tests for agent_mcp_tool with only test_output, with tool_call_transcript, and with contract_check.

findings.description: F003 typed-skip EvidenceRefs specify availability=unavailable and data_provenance=degraded, but do not require data_source, consumer_family, or degraded_mode, which F001/F004 need for validation and per-family degradation checks.
findings.recommendation: Require every F003 typed-skip to populate data_source, consumer_family=agent, and a degraded_mode accepted by the journey when it represents a degraded data source.

findings.description: The no-secret assertion is pinned only for the MCP transcript path, while the required evidence asks harness tests for all three agent adapters to be no-secret. CLI and contract artifacts could leak secret-shaped fields without violating the written F003 acceptance.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same no-secret-shaped-field assertion to CLI transcript and contract-check artifacts, preferably through shared harness validation.

findings.description: F004 describes a pure checker mostly at the journey evidence-set level, but the contract requires human and agent journeys for the same objective to agree by shared data_source key. The objective-level collection and comparison boundary is not pinned.
findings.recommendation: Define whether the checker accepts an objective-level evidence set or add an aggregator that groups journeys by objective and data_source before running cross-family agreement.

findings.description: EvidenceRef data_provenance is optional for compatibility, but F002 does not define how consumer-readiness evidence with an evidence_class and missing data_provenance is handled. That leaves seeded-versus-real enforcement dependent on implementation choices.
findings.recommendation: Specify that evidence lacking data_provenance cannot satisfy consumer-readiness requirements, or add an explicit validation error for missing provenance on typed evidence.
